This is an appeal u/s 372 of Cr.P.C preferred by the appellant/complainant challenging the order of sentence passed in C.C. No.17758/2017 dated 16/11/2021 on the file of XXXI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 2. Rank of the parties is referred to as per their ranks assigned before the trial court.

3. The facts of the case leading to this appeal may be summarized as under:
The complainant and accused are close relatives, father of accused and complainant are brothers.

On 05/03/2017 at about 10 a.m. accused committed criminal trespass by entering into site No.110, Katha No.2371, Bagalagunte, belonging to the complainant and also demolished the common wall, complainant having learnt about the incident rushed near the property, questioned Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 the act of accused and tried to stop him from demolishing the wall, accused created nuisance,
picked up quarrel, abused him in filthy language, caused financial loss to the tune of Rs.15,000/- by demolishing the wall, as such on 05/03/2017 a complaint was lodged against the accused before Bagalagunte police station, hence criminal case came to be registered against him for the offences punishable under Section 448, 504, 506 of IPC.

After due investigation charge sheet came to be filed against accused, as such the trial court framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 448, 504, 427 and 506 of IPC, prosecution examined its witnesses as P.W. 1 to 8 and also exhibited six documents as Ex.P.1 to P.6, after completion of prosecution evidence accused was examined under Section 313 of Cr.P.C, the trial court Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 having framed the points for consideration for the aforementioned offences, arrived at the conclusion that accused is guilty of the charges leveled against him, therefore convicted the accused on 16/11/2021 and at the same time released the accused by applying the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act with a direction that accused shall execute a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with like sum surety, has to keep peace and good behavior for a period of two years, he shall not change his residence, if so he shall intimate the court and investigating officer, he shall not commit any offences within two years, in default he shall suffer sentence of conviction passed in the case and also directed him to pay compensation of Rs.15,000/- to the complainant towards mental agony and damage towards the property.
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 4.

Therefore being aggrieved by the portion of judgment and order dated 16/11/2021 passed in C.C.
No.17758/2018 in so far as passing of order of sentence of 31st ACJM Bengaluru, the complainant has preferred the above criminal appeal urging the following grounds:-
a) The trial court has failed to appreciate the well established principles of law of Indian Penal Code, offences committed by the accused are grievous in nature and court ought to have imposed sentence of imprisonment as well as fine.

sentences.text:
The trial court erred in holding that the accused was first time offender, having small children at home, he is the only earning member of his family, offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, accused has no records of antecedents and further trial court erred in drawing the conclusion that accused would not commit the similar offences once again.
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 c)

It is submitted that, there are several civil cases pending between the complainant and accused, as such there are chances of creating unnecessary trouble to the complainant and his family, the trial court has failed to consider the injustice caused on the complainant and intensity of the offences committed by the accused.

d) Accused is not entitled for concession on the ground that he was a first offender and not granting punishment to the accused would affect the society in large, thus the order of sentence passed by the trial court is bad in law and opposed to settled principles of law, passed mechanically without applying judicial mind.
Hence, it is prayed to set aside the impugned order dated 16/11/2021 passed in C.C. No.17758/2017 by 31st ACJM, Bengaluru.
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 5.
After registration of the appeal, notice was issued to the respondent, appeared through his counsel.
The entire trial court records have been secured.
6. Heard Arguments.
Perused the materials on record and also the written arguments submitted by the respondent.

7. The following points do arise for my consideration;
1) Whether petitioner had sufficient cause for not preferring this appeal within the period of limitation?
2) Whether the trial court is justified in applying the provisions of P.O. Act while passing sentence after the judgment of conviction against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 448,
427, 504 and 506 of IPC in C.C. No.17758/2017 dated 16/11/2021 ?
3) Whether there is legal infirmity in the impugned judgment, which requires interference of this court ?

4) What Order?
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022

sentences.text:
On re-appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, in the light of the arguments advanced by the learned advocates of both sides, my findings on the aforesaid points as follows:-
Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: In the negative Point No.3: In the negative Point No.4: As per final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. POINT No.1: Appellant has filed an application u/s 5 of Limitation Act for condonation of 200 days delay in preferring this appeal.

Perused the application filed u/s Sec. 5 of Limitation Act and contents of affidavit, wherein it is sworn that, after passing of order on 16/11/2021, he was informed by his counsel that, the order of sentence is required to be challenged before the court Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 and instructed to obtain all exhibits, depositions and other relevant documents pertaining to the case to process the same in order to prefer an appeal, due to unavoidable circumstances the appellant could not file the appeal well within the time which is not intentional but for a bonafide reason.

It is further submitted that, the Hon'ble Apex court in an order dated 10/01/2022 passed in Misc. appeal No.21/2022 and Misc. application No.665/2021 in suo moto W.P. No.3/2020 extended the period of limitation in all proceedings for filing of appeals, revision petitions etc., dated 01/01/2022.
In the aforesaid miscellaneous applications of suo moto writ petition and appeal before this court is filed on 12/07/2022.
Above application is strongly resisted by the respondent on the ground of delay by contending that no cogent and sufficient reasons are assigned to condone delay of six months.
Therefore it is Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 prayed to not to condone the delay and reject the application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act.

10. Though the reasons assigned by the appellant is not satisfactory to some extent, however it is stated that he is unable to approach the counsel well in time by obtaining all the certified copies of the judgment, deposition and other material records.
Therefore the reasons assigned by the appellant/complainant to condone the delay in preferring this appeal appears to be genuine and satisfactory.

Moreover the date of judgment and date of preferring the appeal were all on the verge of Covid-19 pandemic situation and it is also true that at that time the Hon'ble Apex court in its suo moto writ petition as mentioned supra has extended the period of limitation.

11. In addition, the Hon'ble Apex court in catena of decisions has laid down that, the court shall take liberal approach in condoning the delay in filing the appeals or Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 petitions.

In AIR 1988 SC 897 (G.Ramegowda V/s. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bengaluru), Hon'ble Apex court pleased to observe that;
'Sufficient cause' in Section 5 must receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice and generally delay in preferring appeals are required to be condoned in the interest of justice where no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bonafides is imputable to the party seeking condonation of the delay.

sentences.text: because it is capable of removing injustice and is expected to do so.'

In the light of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and under the facts and circumstances of the present case, this court opined that, it is just and proper to condone the delay of 200 days in preferring this criminal appeal to provide an opportunity to prosecute the petition.
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022
Hence this interim application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
12. POINT No.2 AND 3 :- These points are interrelated, hence they are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.

13. It is canvassed on behalf of the learned counsel for the appellant/complainant that, though the trial court has passed the judgment of conviction based on the available material evidence, failed to consider the facts that there are number of civil litigation pending amongst complainant and accused and that would trigger him in future to commit similar kind of offences, as such,
consideration of the trial court that accused is not an habitual offender, he is first offender, he is the sole bread earner, having aged parents and children at home is not a ground to set him free without passing sentence of imprisonment and fine on the Crl.
Appeal No.816/2022 accused

. Hence, feeling dissatisfied by the order of sentence passed by the trial court the appellant/complainant prays to set aside the order of sentence and to pass appropriate sentence in accordance with law.

14. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the accused in his written submission contended that,
the appeal is not maintainable under Section 374 of Cr.P.C and the said provision is for the accused to prefer the appeal and not by the complainant, therefore it is prayed to dismiss the same.

Further it is submitted that, the reasons assigned by complainant for condonation of delay is not acceptable,
hence prayed to dismiss the appeal on ground of delay itself.

It is further canvassed that, there are number of civil litigations pending amongst the complainant and accused family, they are close relatives and the complainant inflicting cruelty out of sheer animosity against the accused Crl.
Appeal No.816/2022 who is a central government employee discharging his duty as net working engineer at Indian Institute of Science.

It is submitted that accused has also preferred an appeal against the order of the trial court challenging the judgment of conviction against him and submitted that the application of Probation of Offenders Act by taking into consideration of past, present and future conduct of the respondent is just and proper.

It is alleged that the main intention of the appellant/complainant is to remove the accused from his job, hence it is prayed that the application of the P.O. Act by the trial court is just and proper.
Therefore it is prayed to dismiss the appeal in the interest of justice.
15. In this background, on rival submissions of both sides, this court has given anxious consideration to the materials on record.

sentences.text: In so far as maintainability of the appeal is concerned, it is preferred under Section 372 of Cr.P.C by the complainant himself and the provision of Section 372 of Cr.P.C provides "right to the victim to prefer an appeal against any order passed by the court acquitting the accused or convicting for a lesser offence or imposing inadequate compensation and such appeal shall lie to the court to which an appeal ordinarily lies against the order of conviction of such court".
Under the circumstances, the appeal filed by the complaint is very well maintainable.

17. The first and foremost contention of the complainant is that the trial court while passing the sentence has not considered the factor of pending litigations between himself and the accused,
according to the complainant pending litigation might induce the accused to do similar type of criminal activities in the days ahead.
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 18.
In this case, complainant and accused are close relatives, complainant is the maternal uncle of accused.

On perusal of the judgment of the trial court, it is seen that, the accused was alleged of committing an offence of criminal trespass by unlawfully entering into site bearing No.110, Katha No.2371, situated at Bagalagunte belonging to complainant within the jurisdiction of Bagalagunte police station, when the said act of the accused was questioned by the complainant, he was abused in filthy language by posing dire consequences, therefore complainant lodged the complaint against the accused, accordingly criminal case came to be registered against him, I.O. after completion of investigation submitted his final report opining that there is a prima facie case, as such cognizance of the offences mentioned supra was taken against the accused and the trial court commenced the trial.

During the trial complainant, eye witnesses, mahazar Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 witnesses as well as investigation officer have all supported the case, therefore the trial court by determining each and every points in respect of alleged offences, hold the accused as guilty for the aforementioned offences.

19. From the discussion of judgment, it can be seen that accused is the son of complainant's elder brother, there was a family partition on 08/05/2002 and in the said partition complaint has got eastern side house measuring 30 x 40 square feet, bearing Katha No.237, consisting of a sheet house which was leased out and at the same time his elder brother's property situated and has given it for rent and on 05/03/2017 accused illegally trespassed into the said sheet house and damaged the western wall which came to the knowledge of the complainant through tenant and this has given raise to dispute in question.
It is to be noted that the complainant has no grievance in respect of the judgment passed by the trial court holding the accused Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 as guilty person.

On the other hand, it is the canvas on behalf of the complainant that, the trial court though hold the accused guilty, failed to consider the pending civil litigations amongst each other and showed leniency by applying provision of Probation Offenders Act.
20. In this context, it is relevant to extract the order portion of sentence passed by the trial court after passing of judgment.

sentences.text: Accused is released on PO Act under Section 4 of the said Act on executing PB of Rs.50,000/- with surety for like sum on the following conditions:-
1. He has to keep peace and of good behavior up to two years.

2. He should not change his residence, if he wants to change his residence he has to intimate the same to the court and I.O.
3.
If he commits any offence within two years he has suffer sentence for the conviction passed in this case.
4. As per Section 5 of the P.O. Act accused is hereby directed to pay compensation of Rs.15,000/- to the complainant for mental injury and damage of property.
5. Office is directed to supply free copy of the judgment.
Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 21.

On perusal of the aforesaid order it can be noticed that, the trial court has ordered Rs.15,000/-
as compensation towards damage of property and also for mental agony.
It has taken into consideration the relationship of complainant and accused and also the pending several civil litigations amongst each other.
It can also be seen that, the trial court has considered that the accused is a bread earner of his family having an aged parents and children at home.

Another foremost important factor that was taken into consideration by the trial court while passing the order is that the accused is a first offender and alleged offences are neither punishable with death or life imprisonment.
Thus the trial court has considered the mitigating factors and circumstances while passing order on sentence.
22. It is a fact that accused is not an habitual offender to involve in these kind of activities again and again.

On Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 perusal of written arguments of the respondent, it can be noticed that accused is a central government employee working as net work engineer in TATA Institute of Science from past 10 years, as such the reason assigned by the trial court for application of Probation of Offenders Act appears to be just and proper.
Hence, the ground urged by the complainant are not sustainable.

The trial court while passing the sentence has considered the financial loss said to have been caused on the complainant for demolishing of the common wall by the accused and fairly imposed compensation of Rs.15,000/- to the complainant.
The mitigating circumstances that were considered are the dependents of the accused and their livelihood.
In addition, the fact that accused is a first offender has also been considered along with pending litigations amongst the complainant and himself.
Thus all these, mitigating circumstances might have led the trial court to reduce the Crl. Appeal No.816/2022 severity of sentences which is just and fair.
Under these situation, grounds urged by the complainant have no merits.
The trial court has passed just and fair sentence.
Hence, there are no justifiable reasons to interfere with the order of sentence passed by the trial court.
With these observations, point No.2 and 3 are answered in the Negative.
